railroad-ir.comment: Read the lowercase IR header and its following boundary. railroad.md#shared-scanning-and-header-boundaries: Their only custom keyword is their header. It must end immediately before `%%`, common Notation whitespace or EOF; the boundary is not consumed. Keywords otherwise use exact case.

patterns.comment: Read native hidden YAML. railroad.md#native-hidden-forms: At a unit boundary, hidden-yaml starts with `---`, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs and LF; raw CRLF is equivalent after common line conversion. An optional body ends with LF before the closing `---`. Try the body-present alternative first, taking as few body characters as allow a qualifying closer; only if that fails use the empty-body alternative. Thus adjacent fences can pass an apparent closer and hide intervening rules when a later closer exists.

Read a native hidden directive. railroad.md#native-hidden-forms: A hidden-directive starts with `%%{` and ends at the first `}%%` followed by LF, Notation whitespace or EOF. Consume an immediately following LF; the other boundary characters are only looked at. A closer without that boundary is passed in search of a later qualifying closer. If no native directive matches, native-percent-comment may take its opening line instead.
Read native percent comments. railroad.md#native-comments: A native-percent-comment starts with `%%` and reads to CR/LF or EOF, excluding that line terminator; even bare `%%` qualifies.

Read title and accessibility metadata. railroad.md#metadata-units: All four grammars try title-line, acc-title-line, then acc-descr-line or acc-descr-block before names. A title-line is `title`, optionally followed by exactly one ASCII space/tab separator and line content. Content extends to CR/LF or the first `%%`, whichever comes first. The separator is required for nonempty title content; bare `title` is still a complete unit and has no word boundary.

Read the eight IR constructor keywords. railroad.md#ir-units: IR tries its header first, then the constructors `nonterminal`, `zeroOrMore`, `oneOrMore`, `sequence`, `optional`, `terminal`, `special`, `choice`, then `= ; ( , )`, metadata, ir-name, ir-string, native padding, hidden-yaml, hidden-directive, native-percent-comment and C-comment, in that order. The header and constructors have ir-name as their longer alternative; other punctuation has none.

Read operators, separators and grouping delimiters. railroad.md#ir-units: IR tries its header first, then the constructors `nonterminal`, `zeroOrMore`, `oneOrMore`, `sequence`, `optional`, `terminal`, `special`, `choice`, then `= ; ( , )`, metadata, ir-name, ir-string, native padding, hidden-yaml, hidden-directive, native-percent-comment and C-comment, in that order. The header and constructors have ir-name as their longer alternative; other punctuation has none.

Read quoted strings with the dialect's escape rules. railroad.md#ir-units: An ir-string uses matching single or double quotes. It may be empty and may contain physical line breaks. Read nonquote, nonbackslash characters, or a backslash and one following character, until the matching unescaped quote. The character after a backslash cannot be CR, LF, U+2028 or U+2029. A missing quote rejects; there are no number units in IR.

Read a rule name or reference. railroad.md#ir-units: An ir-name starts with an ASCII letter or underscore and continues with word characters or hyphens, taking as many as possible. A constructor prefix followed by more name characters is a name; an exact constructor cannot be a rule name. The earlier metadata title prefix still takes `title` from a longer name, as described below.

Read an ISO block comment; read directives whole and common comments independently. railroad.md#native-comments: EBNF also has ISO-comment, `(*` through the first `*)`. railroad.md#native-comments: Block comments do not nest, can contain all line-separator characters and require their closer. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

patterns.comment: Read title and accessibility metadata. railroad.md#metadata-units: All four grammars try title-line, acc-title-line, then acc-descr-line or acc-descr-block before names. A title-line is `title`, optionally followed by exactly one ASCII space/tab separator and line content. Content extends to CR/LF or the first `%%`, whichever comes first. The separator is required for nonempty title content; bare `title` is still a complete unit and has no word boundary.

Read special-sequence text, retaining directives and entities. railroad.md#ebnf-units: A special-sequence is `?`, content with no `?` or `;` and at least one nonwhitespace character, then the first `?`. Its content can include physical newlines, U+2028 and U+2029; backslashes and quotes do not protect a closer. Empty or whitespace-only content does not make this unit. A longer special-sequence wins over postfix `?`, so `"a"? "b"?` is a sequence of a string and a special sequence, not two optional strings. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

Read operators, separators and grouping delimiters. railroad.md#ebnf-units: EBNF tries its header, `::=`, `= ; | , ( ) [ ] { } ? * + -`, metadata, ebnf-name, ebnf-string, special-sequence, native padding, hidden-yaml, hidden-directive, native-percent-comment, C-comment and ISO-comment. Its header has ebnf-name as a longer alternative; `(` has ISO-comment, `?` has special-sequence and `-` has hidden-yaml. No other EBNF punctuation has a longer alternative.

Read quoted strings with the dialect's escape rules. railroad.md#ebnf-units: An ebnf-string has matching single or double quotes, can be empty and can contain physical line breaks. A backslash takes exactly the next character except CR, LF, U+2028 and U+2029; an unescaped matching quote closes it. Unclosed strings reject. There is no independent EBNF number unit.

Read a rule name or reference. railroad.md#ebnf-units: An ebnf-name starts with an ASCII letter or underscore and continues maximally with word characters or hyphens. In particular, `A-B` is one name; `A - B` has an exception operator. Without the required colon or brace, an accTitle/accDescr prefix can be a name, whereas the earlier title prefix is taken even from a longer name.

railroad-abnf.comment: Read the lowercase ABNF header and its following boundary. railroad.md#shared-scanning-and-header-boundaries: Their only custom keyword is their header. It must end immediately before `%%`, common Notation whitespace or EOF; the boundary is not consumed. Keywords otherwise use exact case.

patterns.comment: Read an ABNF numeric-value spelling as text, retaining directives. railroad.md#abnf-units: An abnf-numeric-value is `%`, one of `x X d D b B`, a nonempty maximal run of hexadecimal digits, then zero or more `-` or `.` separators each followed by another nonempty run of hexadecimal digits. Here hexadecimal digits are ASCII `0`–`9`, `A`–`F` and `a`–`f`. Do not validate digits against the base letter or range order. Preserve the whole spelling as text; `%x41Z` is followed by a separate reference Z. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

Try the body-present alternative first, taking as few body characters as allow a qualifying closer; only if that fails use the empty-body alternative. Read a native hidden directive. railroad.md#native-hidden-forms: A hidden-directive starts with `%%{` and ends at the first `}%%` followed by LF, Notation whitespace or EOF. Read native percent comments. railroad.md#native-comments: A native-percent-comment starts with `%%` and reads to CR/LF or EOF, excluding that line terminator; even bare `%%` qualifies.

Read ABNF semicolon comments when longer than a terminator. railroad.md#native-comments: In ABNF, semicolon-comment starts with `;` and reads to CR/LF or EOF. Only a match longer than the single-character terminator wins its longer alternative. A bare `;` is therefore punctuation, whereas `;` followed by a space or other line text becomes a comment, including where a rule terminator was intended.

patterns.comment: Read title and accessibility metadata. railroad.md#metadata-units: All four grammars try title-line, acc-title-line, then acc-descr-line or acc-descr-block before names. A title-line is `title`, optionally followed by exactly one ASCII space/tab separator and line content. Content extends to CR/LF or the first `%%`, whichever comes first. The separator is required for nonempty title content; bare `title` is still a complete unit and has no word boundary.

Read ABNF repeat bounds and a separate repeat operator. railroad.md#abnf-units: An abnf-count is a maximal nonempty run of ASCII decimal digits. A star-repeat consists of an optional count, `*`, and an optional count; an exact-repeat consists of one count. Ordinary whitespace and native hidden forms cannot occur within either repeat, but can occur between a complete repeat and its primary. Both counts may be omitted, and leading zeroes are allowed. railroad.md#common-directive-and-semicolon-boundaries: The pieces of an ABNF repeat are its decimal bounds and star, even though native matching requires them to be adjacent.

Read operators, separators and grouping delimiters. railroad.md#abnf-units: ABNF tries its header, `= ; / ( ) [ ]`, metadata, abnf-name, abnf-string, abnf-numeric-value, star-repeat, exact-repeat, native padding, hidden-yaml, hidden-directive, native-percent-comment and semicolon-comment. Its header has abnf-name as a longer alternative; `;` has semicolon-comment. There are no other longer alternatives.

Read quoted strings with the dialect's escape rules. railroad.md#abnf-units: An abnf-string starts with a double quote and takes every character through the next double quote; it can be empty and include physical newlines, U+2028 and U+2029. Backslash is ordinary content and never protects a quote. Single quotes and a missing closing double quote reject.

Read a rule name or reference. railroad.md#abnf-units: An abnf-name starts with an ASCII letter, then takes as many ASCII letters, digits or hyphens as possible. Underscores and non-ASCII letters are not name characters. The earlier metadata prefix rules apply before names, including references.

U+2028 and U+2029 do not terminate native line comments. Hash comments are not IR, EBNF or ABNF comments; C comments are not ABNF or PEG comments, and ISO comments are EBNF-only.

PEG has no number unit.

Read a rule name or reference. railroad.md#peg-units: A peg-name starts with an ASCII letter or underscore and continues maximally with word characters or hyphens. Metadata is tried before names, so title-prefixed references reject but accTitle-prefixed references without a colon can be names.
